medicina.titulo: Three studies reveal the hidden layers between DNA and disease
medicina.resumo: In three studies published in Nature today, Australian researchers have made advances in our understanding of how genetic differences between people influence disease. The team from the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, in collaboration with the Murdoch Children's Research Institute, UNSW and other partners, linked genetic risk regions for 16 diseases to possible causes in specific immune cells, identifying nearly 1,500 genes that may contribute to a range of diseases. These discoveries are set to accelerate drug development and precision medicine across many diseases, ranging from cancers to immune and neurological conditions.

medicina.titulo: Mindfulness-based therapy may reshape brain responses to opioid cues during addiction treatment
medicina.resumo: Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE), a behavioral therapy used alongside medication treatment, may help people with opioid use disorder respond differently to drug-related cues and natural rewards, according to a randomized clinical trial led by researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. The findings offer insight into how MORE may reduce opioid craving and support recovery.

medicina.titulo: Arsenic drug combo resurrects 'guardian of the genome' to fight aggressive blood cancers
medicina.resumo: A combination cancer therapy that relies on the reactivation of a tumor suppressor protein to kill leukemic and other blood cancer cells has shown promise in a small pilot trial.

medicina.titulo: How the tumor environment influences bowel cancer cells' behavior and chemotherapy response
medicina.resumo: New research led by experts at the University of Nottingham has revealed how collagen in the tumor environment can alter bowel cancer cell behavior and influence inflammatory responses to chemotherapy, highlighting potential new avenues for future research into cancer treatment. The findings, published in the Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research, highlight the importance of the environment surrounding cancer cells in shaping how they behave and respond to treatment.

biologia.titulo: Three-quarters of NFL football players may end up with CTE
biologia.resumo: The first estimate of CTE prevalence across the NFL suggests 75 percent of players may suffer from the neurodegenerative disease.

biologia.titulo: Japan's genome-editing law sets a global ethics challenge
biologia.resumo: A Hiroshima University researcher contends that Japan's newly enacted law regulating human genome-edited embryos and germ cells marks a significant advance in the governance of reproductive genome editing. Tsutomu Sawai, professor at Hiroshima University's Graduate School of Humanities and Social Sciences, praises the new law for defining prohibited activities and penalties for violation but also stresses the need for stronger international coordination to prevent the prohibitions from being circumvented by individuals seeking procedures abroad.

biologia.titulo: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software

robotica.resumo: A team of University of Toronto Engineering researchers has developed a flexible foot pad for the "Hopcopter"—a one-legged, hopping robot they developed—significantly enhancing its performance on sand, ice and other difficult terrain.

robotica.titulo: WorldOracle Tests Whether World Models Can Reliably Predict Real-World Executions
robotica.resumo: In one case showcased by WorldOracle, a robot's grasp missed, yet the world model predicted that the robot had successfully picked up the fruit. The post WorldOracle Tests Whether World Models Can Reliably Predict Real-World Executions appeared first on The Robot Report .

robotica.titulo: Insect-inspired flying robot bounces back after collisions
robotica.resumo: Flying insects, such as fruit flies, bees, dragonflies and mosquitoes, can dart through narrow spaces and survive collisions with various objects. In contrast, many flying robots fall, suffer damage or even break down when they hit nearby surfaces or objects.

software.titulo: Claude trava tarefas de engenharia reversa e revolta quem modifica jogos e TVs
software.resumo: O Claude começou a interromper tarefas de engenharia reversa de softwares, jogos e firmwares de smart TVs. Os usuários relatam, em publicação no Reddit, que o assistente de inteligência artificial inicia o processamento dos pedidos, mas interrompe a execução após acionar filtros de segurança que restringem determinadas atividades. As reclamações ganharam força após uma publicação do usuário u/targaryenNotJon na comunidade r/ClaudeAI, no Reddit. Segundo ele, o filtro de segurança do Claude foi acionado quando o usuário pediu a engenharia reversa de uma Smart TV, mas não bloqueou a mesma tarefa aplicada a um videogame. No entanto, outros relatos também citam restrições em projetos de análise de programas e adaptação de jogos para navegadores. As restrições provocaram críticas de desenvolvedores , que acusam a empresa de limitar modificações legítimas em softwares e equipamentos. Uma parte dos usuários também questiona se os filtros prejudicam o direito de reparar e personalizar dispositivos próprios. software.titulo: [$] The campaign to push Northstar into Linux distributions
software.resumo: There is not a broad selection of mature, open-source web-browser engines for Linux users. Most of the browsers available for Linux are based on one of just three projects: Chromium's Blink , Firefox's Gecko , or WebKit . A new entrant would generally be seen as a welcome alternative, but the recent campaign to push one of the LLM-written Nordstjernen browsers into Debian and Arch Linux has raised some questions about the project's development and security processes.

Security updates have been issued by AlmaLinux (emacs, thunderbird, and xdg-dbus-proxy), Debian (bind9, openjdk-21, pdns, php-mongodb, and thunderbird), Fedora (brotli, chromium, clevis, eog, flatpak, ghostscript, kernel, libinstpatch, libreswan, mingw-freetype, mingw-gstreamer1, mingw-gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free, mingw-gstreamer1-plugins-base, mingw-gstreamer1-plugins-good, openssh, perl-Alien-Brotli, perl-DBI, python3.12, rust-onefetch, stargz-snapshotter, util-linux, and webkitgtk), Mageia (cifs-utils, libxml2, packages, perl-Cpanel-JSON-XS, perl-Text-CSV_XS, sogo, util-linux, and weechat), Oracle (brotli, firefox, flatpak, gcc-toolset-15-gcc, kernel, libreswan, nodejs:22, nodejs:24, python-urllib3, skopeo, and xdg-dbus-proxy), Slackware (proftpd), SUSE (azure-storage-azcopy, containerd, corepack24, grok-build, ImageMagick, libsoup-2_4-1, matrix-synapse, podman, psqlODBC, python, python-M2Crypto-doc, python-Twisted-doc, and xen), and Ubuntu (authd).

astrofisica.titulo: NASA systems engineering team details Habitable Worlds Observatory mission architecture
astrofisica.resumo: Finding an Earth-like world beyond the solar system is the holy grail of exoplanet research, and the field has seen remarkable technological advances in detecting and studying exoplanets since the first confirmed exoplanet around a sun-like star was discovered in 1995. These advances include ground- and space-based telescopes, notably the James Webb Space Telescope. Although astronomers have already directly imaged some exoplanets, directly imaging Earth-like planets around sun-like stars remains a major technological challenge, primarily because these planets are extremely faint compared with their host stars and appear very close to them in the sky.

In this Webb image released on Oct. 22, 2026, we see a turbulent cauldron of star formation filled with dense clumps of gas. This region is named N159 and is located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This region has a lower metallicity […]

astrofisica.titulo: Dead star and planetary bodies: astronomers spot unique disc of debris that foretells Solar System’s future
astrofisica.resumo: Astronomers using the European Southern Observatory’s Very Large Telescope (ESO’s VLT) have found a rare disc of debris around a dead star that provides a glimpse of what may happen to our Solar System. Unlike in similar systems previously found, the debris — the leftovers of planets that once orbited the star — is organised in a double disc, the two parts separated by a clear gap. The disc appears to be shaped by two planetary bodies, one possibly as big as Pluto, that have survived the violent death of the star.

Such operations typically take several tens of nanoseconds in superconducting quantum computers. The paper was published in Nature Communications.

computadores_pessoais.titulo: Windows File History broken? How to fix it and restore your files
computadores_pessoais.resumo: Did you know that Windows can automatically back up your files to an external drive or network share? SO if your SSD fails or you need to reinstall Windows, you can quickly restore your files. It’s called File History. If File History isn’t working, there are two possible reasons. First, you may have forgotten to enable it, as it’s disabled by default in Windows. Second, there may be configuration issues. In this case, resetting the feature might help. You can access File History through the Control Panel. In the icon view, click the File History icon. Then, on the left-hand side, click Select Drive and choose a backup destination. An external drive is a good option. If you want to store your files on a network share, click the Add Network Address link. Confirm your selection by clicking OK. To start the backup, click Run Now in the File History start window. If File History stops working because of a configuration error, you can delete its configuration data. Your backup files should remain on the backup drive. In File Explorer, navigate to the folder C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\FileHistory. Delete the Data and Configuration folders. Note: The Configuration

computadores_pessoais.titulo: Windows 11 search can now skip web results and focus on your PC
computadores_pessoais.resumo: When searching for an application via the Start menu in Windows 11, users often receive not only local results but also web suggestions. These appear alongside the apps and documents you’re searching for, leading to Edge. Microsoft now offers a way to disable such web results. As reported by Windows Latest , the new setting is now rolling out to more Windows 11 PCs. Microsoft began the phased rollout in August 2026, and despite widening, the feature is not yet available to all users. How to disable web results in Windows 11 If the new setting is available on your computer, you can disable web search as follows: Open the Windows 11 Settings . Go to Privacy & security → Search . Within the “Indexing status” section, look for the setting called “Show suggested search results.” Toggle off the option for web searches. If required, you can also disable suggestions from the Microsoft Store. Open Windows Search again for the change to take effect. If the setting is missing, you can enable the “Get the latest updates as soon as they’re available” option under Settings → Windows Update . This allows new features to arrive on your PC sooner. ciberseguranca.titulo: Golpe do falso Claude usa site oficial da Anthropic para roubar senhas e criptomoedas
ciberseguranca.resumo: Uma campanha de cibercriminosos usa anúncios pagos do Google para distribuir versões falsas do Claude e roubar senhas e criptomoedas. A fraude direciona usuários a páginas hospedadas no domínio oficial da Anthropic, claude.ai, para enganar as vítimas e instalar programas maliciosos em computadores com macOS e Windows. A fraude foi identificada por pesquisadores da Gen Digital, empresa responsável pelas marcas Norton e Avast. Os criminosos exploram duas ferramentas do Claude, chamadas Artefatos e chats compartilhados , que permitem publicar conteúdos acessíveis por outras pessoas. Com elas, os invasores criam páginas falsas dentro do próprio site da inteligência artificial, o que dificulta a identificação do golpe pelo endereço da página. As páginas mostram apenas um aviso discreto de que o conteúdo foi criado por um usuário e não passou por verificação. No macOS, a vítima recebe instruções para executar um comando no Terminal , que instala o Atomic Stealer (AMOS), um malware especializado no roubo de informações. O aparelho apareceu de forma discreta no site oficial da fabricante em alguns países europeus e também chama atenção pela câmera principal de 108 MP e pela tela de 120 Hz. O preço oficial ficou acima do que vazamentos anteriores indicavam e a ficha técnica traz apenas 4 GB de memória RAM, mesmo em uma faixa na qual a própria Motorola oferece alternativas mais bem equipadas. 📱 Veja as melhores promoções de celulares no WhatsApp do CT Ofertas Bateria de 7.000 mAh é o grande destaque A bateria é o principal diferencial do Moto G47 Power.
